artifact.short: The file a completed export produces — CSV or JSON, written to the directory you configured.

backfill.short: The background pass that fills a slot column with values read out of already-stored JSON payloads.

backfill-window.short: The interval between a schema operation returning and its background pass finishing — the period during which the change is declared but not yet applied to stored data.

bounded-read.short: The two-query strategy behind every read and search: the first query finds only the matching entry IDs, and the second fetches the full rows for just those IDs.

bulk-ingestion.short: Writing many entries in one call, committed in chunks rather than as one giant transaction.

chronicler.short: The daemon that turns export jobs into files, streaming CSV or JSON to disk.

compaction.short: The operator-initiated repack that relocates a model's filterable fields onto the fewest pages that can hold them.

correlation-id.short: An identifier that ties every log event belonging to one operation together, including events a daemon emits minutes later in a different process.

cursor.short: The opaque token that marks your position in a paginated read — there is no offset parameter and no total count.

daemon.short: Background work that keeps filtering caught up, run either as a long-lived process or in bounded bursts from a schedule — StarDust ships four, coordinating only through the database.

dead-letter-queue.short: Where the Reconciler parks an individual record it could not process, so one bad row cannot wedge the whole queue.

declared-type.short: The type you register a field as — string, int, numeric, or datetime.

demotion.short: Marking a previously filterable field as non-filterable, which takes effect immediately.

entry.short: One record of a model, belonging to one tenant.

exhaustion-fallback.short: What happens when you write a filterable field and no slot capacity is available: the value still lands in the JSON payload and the write succeeds.

export-job.short: A request to dump a model's entries to a file, handled asynchronously so a large extract never ties up a request.

extension-page.short: A side table holding the indexed slot columns that mirror filterable field values, joined 1:1 to the entry table.

field.short: One named attribute of a model, with a declared type and a filterable flag.

filter-tree.short: The structure a filter takes: individual conditions combined with AND, OR, and NOT into a tree of any depth.

filterable.short: The flag that decides whether a field gets a slot and can therefore be used in filters and sorts.

idempotency-key.short: An optional string you attach to an asynchronous bulk submission so retrying it never ingests the same batch twice.

index-headroom.short: The number of spare indexed columns built into every new extension page, so a handful of fields promoted in sequence land together rather than scattering.

indexed.short: Whether a field's slot is live right now — that is, whether a filter on it would actually work.

liberator.short: The daemon that reclaims slots freed by demoted or deleted fields, clearing their old values before returning them to the free pool.

model.short: A named data shape within a tenant — the rough equivalent of a table, except you define it at runtime.

payload.short: The complete JSON object holding all of an entry's field values — the authoritative system of record.

pre-flight-rejection.short: The engine's policy of refusing an impossible query at the API boundary, before the database is touched at all.

promotion.short: Turning a non-filterable field into a filterable one on a live system.

queryfilter.short: The JSON wire format for filters, so a filter can travel from a browser or an API client and be validated before it reaches your database.

reconciler.short: The daemon that does the catching up — it drains every kind of deferred work the engine produces, in bounded chunks.

retype.short: Changing a field's declared type on a live system, converting its existing values in the background.

schema-registry.short: The set of tables recording your models, fields, pages, and slot assignments — the engine's own bookkeeping.

schema-version.short: A single counter bumped every time coordination-relevant registry state changes, so a live schema change can be picked up without restarting your application.

search-driver.short: The swappable component that actually executes a filtered read — MySQL by default, or your own to delegate to an external search service.

slot.short: One typed, indexed column on an extension page that mirrors one filterable field's value.

soft-deletion.short: How deleting an entry works: a timestamp is set rather than the row removed.

sort.short: The ordering of a read — by entry ID, creation time, or a single indexed field.

spread.short: How many extension pages a single model's filterable slots are scattered across, and therefore how many extra joins a filtered query pays.

sync-queue.short: The small table holding entries whose indexed mirroring was deferred, almost always because of an exhaustion fallback.

system-of-record.short: The authoritative copy of your data — always the JSON payload, never the indexed slots.

tenant.short: The top-level isolation boundary: every query the engine builds carries the tenant ID, so one tenant's data is unreachable from another's.

tombstoned-slot.short: A slot whose field is gone but whose old values are still physically in the column, and so cannot yet be reused.

vertical-schema-partitioning.short: The architecture behind StarDust: each entry is split across a complete JSON payload for storage and separate indexed slot columns for querying.

watcher.short: The daemon that keeps slot capacity ahead of demand, provisioning new extension pages before you run out.
